mission_1.search: On the open map, BFS found a path length of 13.5 meters and expanded 928 nodes while A* also found a path length of 13.5 meters, but expanded only 700 nodes. A* examined 228 fewer nodes. I think this is due to the fact that BFS uses a queue with `popleft()` which means t explores cells in the order they were discovered. Meanwhile, A* uses a priority queue with `heappop()` and calculates `f = g + h`. This helps A* prioritize cells that make the shortest path while expanding fewer nodes.
mission_1.failure: On the constrained map, BFS found a path of 24.5 meters and expanded 848 nodes, DFS found a path of 104 meters ans expanded 524 nodes, and IDDFS reached the limit with 250,001 nodes. This is because BFS uses a FIFO queue while DFS uses a LIFO stack. IDDFS reached the resource limit after 250,001 expansions because it kept runs depth-limited DFS making it explore many of the same cells again. On the unreachable map, all four algorithms (BFS, DFS, IDDFS, and A*) returned `no_path`. This means they finished searching and determined that no valid route existed. In contrast, `resource_limit` means the algorithm stopped because it exceeded its allowed resources before completing the search, so it does not prove that no path exists. I used AI to understand the algorithms while writing some of the Python implementations making sure to explain how the code works. I reviewed and tweaked the code and ran the six small tests for each algorithm.
